subject: IB
title: Introduction to Plant Biology
degreeAttributes: Nat Sci & Tech - Life Sciences course.

sections.sectionText: Plants, particularly flowering plants, cover the earth surface, and convert solar energy to chemical energy through photosynthesis, providing raw materials as the sources of food, feed, fuel, clothing, and shelter. Humanity and civilization depend on plants. Plant biology is the scientific study of plants and their relationship with the environment. This course provides comprehensive coverage of plant cells, organs, growth, reproduction, anatomy, morphology, taxonomy, genetics, and ecology. Laboratory and greenhouse experiences complement classroom activities. This course is aimed at helping students to understand and appreciate the complexity and relationships of living systems and the role of plants in the society and environment.

sections.sectionText: Examines theory and practice of curation and management of scientific collections, including archaeological, biological, paleontological, and geological collections. Students gain insight into the nature and importance of collections and explore the profession within the modern collections landscape. Focus placed on comparison of collections, with practical hands-on experience in the University of Illinois’s scientific surveys (ISAS, INHS, and ISGS). Topics covered include physical curation and conservation of collections objects (specimens and artifacts), digital imaging and databasing, and data management.

Pandemics (global outbreaks of infectious disease) are among the most impactful events in human history. Through this course, we will study the major historical and modern pandemics from an advanced biological as well as social and political perspectives. We will compare past pandemics to the public health crisis caused by COVID-19, and we will apply this knowledge to interpret scientific discoveries related to future pandemics and their prevention.
